item.title: Financing Sustainable and Just Transitions: Mechanisms, Accountability and Value Creation
item.content:encoded:
While sustainable finance has expanded as a tool for climate action and capital mobilisation, research has largely focused on aggregate flows rather than how mechanisms are structured and governed. This gap limits understanding of who benefits, how risks are distributed, and whether financial flows reach vulnerable populations or concentrate benefits among well-capitalised actors.

The special issue interrogates institutional practices, governance structures, and implementation processes shaping sustainable finance outcomes. It addresses critical questions about fund allocation decisions, accountability, inclusion of local communities, and adaptability of financial models across diverse contexts, particularly in the Global South.

This collection invites theoretical, empirical, and policy-oriented research reconceptualising sustainable finance as a process of value creation and accountability. The goal is to scrutinise governance frameworks, distributional effects, and capacity to support genuinely fair and inclusive transitions across different contexts.

item.title: Technology, Corporate Governance, and Innovative Management Practices for Sustainable Transformation and Responsible Society
item.content:encoded:
Pieter-Jan Bezemer, Edith Cowan University

Wai Ching Poon, Taylor's University

Sitong Michelle Chen, Auckland University of Technology

Digital technologies enable organizations to pursue sustainability and social objectives, but rapid advancement creates governance challenges around cybersecurity, privacy, algorithmic bias, and transparency. New governance models are needed to balance opportunities and risks in digital transformation.

Current research emphasizes organizational outcomes while neglecting internal processes and managerial innovations that enable responsible technological change. The special issue addresses underexplored concerns about power imbalances, exclusion, inequality, and fairness in digital transformation.

The collection integrates previously separated research on technological disruption, governance, and sustainability. It welcomes interdisciplinary studies exploring how organizations can responsibly integrate technological innovation while addressing governance challenges and fostering sustainable societies.
